enriched_description: Wild goat measuring 70-100 cm at withers weighing 30-100 kg. Body covered with short coarse fur in brown, gray, or reddish coloration with lighter underparts. Males possess large recurved horns with prominent transverse ridges curving backward and upward measuring up to 1 m. Females have smaller horns. Head elongated with beard on chin. Eyes amber with horizontal rectangular pupils. Ears short and pointed. Body agile and muscular adapted for steep mountainous terrain. Legs sturdy with specialized cloven hooves providing grip on rock. Tail short. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

Large African antelope measuring 120-150 cm at shoulder weighing 100-200 kg. Body covered with short reddish-brown to tawny fur with darker legs. Head elongated and narrow with distinctive lyre-shaped horns curving backward then upward. Horns ringed and ridged. Eyes positioned high on head. Ears long and pointed. Body lean and athletic with sloping back. Legs long and slender with dark stockings. Tail long with black tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, short hair insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Grazing antelope of open savanna.

Medium African antelope measuring 75-95 cm at shoulder weighing 40-75 kg. Body covered with short smooth reddish-brown fur with white underparts and distinctive black markings on flanks and tail. Males possess ridged lyre-shaped horns curving backward measuring 45-90 cm. Head narrow with large dark eyes and white eye rings. Ears pointed with black tips. Body slender and athletic. Legs long and slender with black markings on hind legs. Tail white with black stripe. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, short hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Known for enormous leaps exceeding 3 m height.

Small swift antelope measuring 55-110 cm at shoulder weighing 15-85 kg. Body covered with short smooth fur in tan, reddish-brown, or fawn coloration with white underparts and distinctive dark lateral stripe. Both sexes possess slender ringed horns curving backward and slightly inward. Head narrow with large dark lustrous eyes. Ears long and pointed. Body slender and graceful with athletic build. Legs long and slender with black markings. Tail short with black tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, short hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Extremely agile with pronking behavior.

Large camelid measuring 180-230 cm at shoulder weighing 300-600 kg. Single prominent hump on back composed of fat reservoir. Body covered with short sandy-brown to cream-colored fur. Head elongated with long flexible neck. Eyes large with double row of eyelashes. Nostrils slit-like and closable. Upper lip split. Legs long and slender with broad padded feet adapted for sand. Tail short with tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Desert-adapted with water conservation physiology. One-humped camel of hot deserts.

South American camelid measuring 100-120 cm at shoulder weighing 130-200 kg. Body covered with long dense woolly coat in white, brown, black, or piebald coloration. Head elongated with long curved neck. Ears long and banana-shaped. Eyes large and dark. No upper incisors. Body slender without hump (distinguishing from camel). Legs long and slender with two-toed padded feet. Tail short. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, wool insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Smaller than camel lacking hump. Domesticated pack animal of Andean regions.

Small carnivorous mammal measuring 15-30 cm body length weighing 25-250 g. Body extremely elongated and slender with short legs. Fur short and dense in brown dorsally with white or yellow ventral coloration. Some species turn white in winter (ermite morph). Head small and triangular with pointed snout. Eyes small and dark. Ears short and rounded. Neck elongated. Tail short relative to body length. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Carnivorous with high metabolic rate. Elongated body enables pursuit of prey in burrows.

Semiaquatic mustelid measuring 30-50 cm body length weighing 0.5-1.5 kg. Body elongated and slender with short legs. Fur dense, soft, and glossy in dark brown to black coloration. Head small with pointed snout. Eyes small and dark. Ears short and rounded. Tail moderately long (one-third body length). Feet partially webbed with retractile claws. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, dense waterproof fur, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Semiaquatic lifestyle with swimming ability. Valued for luxurious fur.

Mustelid measuring 35-50 cm body length weighing 0.5-1.5 kg. Body elongated with short legs. Fur dark brown to black with lighter facial mask and pale underparts. Head broad with pointed snout. Eyes small and dark. Ears short and rounded. Tail moderately long and bushy. Anal glands produce intensely malodorous fluid ejected when threatened. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Nocturnal woodland carnivore. Defensive scent gland secretion contains thiols and thioacetates.

Mustelid measuring 35-55 cm body length weighing 0.7-1.4 kg. Body elongated and slender with short legs. Fur pale yellowish-brown dorsally with white underparts. Distinctive black facial mask across eyes. Feet, legs, and tail tip black. Head small with pointed snout. Eyes dark. Ears short and rounded. Tail bushy. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Prairie-dwelling carnivore specialized on prairie dog prey. Critically endangered species with captive breeding programs.
